summary: Resolve project settings from the Git root
body: When `target` is a subdirectory of a repository, `repoOf(target)` later treats it as the same project, but this call uses the subdirectory as the config root. It misses the repository-root `.postmaster/settings.toml` (or errors when there is no global config), so front-door can select the global postmaster instead of the project override. Resolve the Git top-level before loading settings.

summary: Pass the project to standalone host launches
body: Project-specific limits are loaded only when `--project` is supplied. The postmaster command in [skills/postmaster/SKILL.md#L259-L261] passes it only to the child `launch`, and the watcher command in [skills/postmaster/harnesses.md#L629-L632] omits it, so those host processes use global/default limits. Pass `--project` to the outer `host run` calls.

summary: Keep projects_roots out of local overrides
body: If `settings.toml` contains `projects_roots`, this function retains it and the merge replaces the global value. `project-settings effective` and the recorded run config then report project roots even though they must come from the global config, as documented in [AGENTS.md#L244-L249]. Exclude this key from the local overlay.

Local settings are never scanned for credentials (the read path also passes `false`), and validation accepts nested config fields such as `tracker.api_key`. Such a value enters the effective config and `run.json`, and can be committed with a tracked settings file, despite [settings.example.toml#L6-L7] requiring keys to stay in env files. Preserve local path allowances while rejecting credential fields and values.
